title: Unconventional Machining Process
quiz_title: Quiz 1: Introduction & Mechanical Energy Based Processes

questions.question: Non-traditional machining processes are used when:

options.B: Material is too hard/brittle or geometry too complex for conventional methods
options.C: Cost needs to be minimized always
options.D: MRR needs to be very high always

questions.question: Non-traditional machining processes are also known as:

options.B: Modern / advanced machining processes

questions.question: In conventional machining, material removal occurs mainly by:

options.B: Shear deformation (chip formation) using a harder tool

questions.question: Non-traditional machining processes are broadly classified based on:

options.B: Type of energy used for material removal

questions.question: Based on the type of energy employed, NTM processes are classified into:

options.A: Mechanical, thermal, electrical, chemical energy based processes
options.B: Only mechanical and thermal

questions.question: Which of the following is a mechanical energy based NTM process?

options.B: USM

questions.question: Which of the following is a thermal energy based NTM process?

options.B: AWJM

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical energy based NTM process?

options.B: USM

questions.question: Which of the following is an electrochemical energy based NTM process?

options.B: AJM

questions.question: NTM processes are generally preferred for machining:

options.B: Hard, brittle, exotic materials and complex shapes

questions.question: A major advantage of non-traditional machining is:

options.B: Ability to machine any hardness of material and produce complex/intricate shapes

questions.question: A general limitation of non-traditional machining processes is:

options.A: Higher MRR than conventional machining always
options.B: Generally lower MRR and higher equipment/operating cost

questions.question: In NTM processes, tool wear is generally:

options.B: Absent or of a different nature compared to conventional cutting tool wear

questions.question: Non-traditional machining processes came into prominence mainly due to development of:

options.B: Aerospace, nuclear and electronics industries needing difficult-to-machine materials/complex shapes

questions.question: Which material typically requires NTM due to difficulty in conventional machining?

options.B: Titanium alloys, superalloys, and ceramics

questions.question: In NTM processes, 'process parameters' refers to:

options.A: Only the cost of the machine
options.B: Variables (pressure, voltage, feed rate, etc.) controlling MRR, accuracy and finish

questions.question: Material Removal Rate (MRR) indicates:

options.A: Volume/mass of material removed per unit time
options.B: Surface roughness

questions.question: Selection of a suitable NTM process depends on:

options.A: Only the cost of the machine
options.B: Workpiece material, shape complexity, required accuracy/finish and MRR

questions.question: Compared to conventional machining, non-traditional machining generally involves:

options.A: Direct mechanical contact and chip formation only
options.B: No conventional chip formation (erosion, dissolution, vaporization, etc.)

questions.question: Hybrid machining processes combine:

options.A: Two or more traditional processes only
options.B: Two or more machining processes (conventional and/or non-conventional) to enhance performance

questions.question: A primary reason for the need for NTM processes is:

options.A: Increasing demand for complex 3D shapes and micro-features difficult with conventional tools
options.B: Decreasing industrial demand

questions.question: Classifying NTM processes by source of energy helps in:

options.A: Understanding the material removal mechanism of each process
options.B: Selling the machines

questions.question: Non-traditional processes are more suitable than conventional processes for:

options.A: Mass production of simple shapes in soft materials
options.B: Precision machining of hard/brittle materials and intricate geometries

questions.question: A key limitation shared by most NTM processes is:

options.A: Very low capital and operating cost
options.B: Relatively low MRR and high initial investment
options.D: Inability to machine any hard material

questions.question: Applications of non-traditional machining processes include:

options.A: Aerospace components, medical implants, micro-electronics and die/mold making
options.B: Only kitchen utensils

questions.question: In Abrasive Jet Machining, material removal occurs due to:

options.B: Erosion caused by high-velocity abrasive particles impacting the workpiece

questions.question: The carrier gas used in AJM is typically:

options.B: Air, nitrogen, or carbon dioxide

questions.question: Commonly used abrasive materials in AJM include:

options.B: Sand only

questions.question: Typical abrasive grain size used in AJM ranges around:

options.B: 1-2 mm

questions.question: The nozzle in AJM is usually made of:

options.B: Tungsten carbide or sapphire (wear-resistant material)

questions.question: Typical standoff distance (nozzle tip to workpiece) in AJM is around:

options.B: 1 to 2 meters

questions.question: AJM is best suited for machining:

options.A: Soft ductile metals like aluminum in bulk
options.B: Hard and brittle materials like glass, ceramics, and semiconductors

questions.question: In AJM, material removal rate mainly depends on:

options.A: Gas pressure, abrasive flow rate, nozzle diameter, standoff distance, grain size
options.B: Only the color of the abrasive

questions.question: Increasing the standoff distance beyond the optimum value in AJM generally:

options.B: Decreases MRR and increases the machining spot size, reducing accuracy

questions.question: AJM is commonly used for:

options.B: Cleaning, deburring, cutting thin sections, drilling fine holes in brittle materials, frosting glass

questions.question: One major limitation of AJM is:

options.B: Low MRR and possible stray cutting (poor accuracy for sharp corners)

questions.question: In AJM, the abrasive particles are propelled by:

options.B: A carrier gas at high pressure/velocity

questions.question: Typical gas pressure used in AJM ranges about:

options.B: 100 to 200 bar

questions.question: AJM is generally NOT suitable for machining:

options.B: Soft, ductile metals (abrasive embedding and low MRR)

questions.question: The mixing ratio in AJM refers to:

options.A: Ratio of abrasive to carrier gas flow rate
options.B: Ratio of nozzle diameter to standoff distance
options.C: Ratio of workpiece hardness to tool hardness

questions.question: Nozzle wear in AJM is caused by:

options.B: Continuous impact/abrasion by abrasive particles passing through it

questions.question: Advantages of AJM include:

options.A: Ability to machine brittle, heat-sensitive materials without much heat, producing intricate shapes
options.B: Highest MRR among all NTM processes

questions.question: In AJM, an increase in abrasive flow rate up to an optimum value:

options.B: Increases MRR up to an optimum point, beyond which it may decrease
options.D: Only affects surface finish, not MRR

questions.question: AJM is often used in the electronics industry for:

options.B: Trimming/cutting thin silicon wafers and semiconductor materials

questions.question: The velocity of abrasive particles in AJM is typically in the range of:
In AJM, a smaller nozzle diameter generally results in:

options.A: A wider machining area with lower accuracy
options.B: A finer, more concentrated jet giving better accuracy for fine work

questions.question: Surface finish obtained by AJM is generally:

options.B: Reasonably good, suitable for fine finishing/frosting

questions.question: AJM cannot be effectively used for very deep cuts because:

options.A: The abrasive jet diverges and MRR drops with depth, introducing taper
options.B: The gas becomes very expensive

questions.question: In AJM, the nozzle tip typically has an orifice of:

options.B: 10 to 20 cm diameter

questions.question: Abrasive Jet Machining removes material predominantly through:

options.A: A micro-chipping/erosion mechanism due to particle impact
options.B: Melting and vaporization

questions.question: In Abrasive Water Jet Machining, the carrier medium for abrasive particles is:

options.B: High-pressure water jet

questions.question: Typical water pressure used in AWJM ranges around:
The abrasive commonly used in AWJM is:

options.B: Table salt

questions.question: In AWJM, abrasive particles are usually introduced into the water jet:

options.A: Before the water reaches the pump
options.B: Downstream of the nozzle in a mixing chamber, entrained by the high-velocity jet

questions.question: AWJM can be used to cut:

options.B: A wide range of materials including metals, composites, ceramics, glass, and stone

questions.question: Compared to AJM, AWJM generally provides:

options.B: Higher MRR and can cut thicker sections with less thermal damage

questions.question: A major advantage of AWJM is:

options.A: It produces a significant heat-affected zone (HAZ)
options.B: It produces little to no HAZ (cold cutting process)
options.C: It can only cut soft plastics

questions.question: The high-pressure pump used in AWJM is typically:

options.B: An intensifier or direct-drive high-pressure pump

questions.question: In AWJM, standoff distance and traverse speed affect:

options.B: Cutting quality, kerf width, and taper of the cut
options.D: Only the color of the finish

questions.question: The mixing/focusing tube in AWJM is generally made of:

options.B: Tungsten carbide or composite carbide (wear resistant)

questions.question: AWJM is widely used in industries such as:

options.B: Only bakery industry

questions.question: One limitation of AWJM is:

options.A: Very high noise and no water usage
options.B: High capital cost, water disposal issues, and possible tapering of cut edges
options.C: Inability to ever cut thick materials

questions.question: In AWJM, the abrasive flow rate affects:

options.B: Material removal rate and surface finish

questions.question: Increasing traverse speed in AWJM beyond the optimum generally leads to:

options.B: Incomplete cutting, increased taper, and rougher surface finish

questions.question: AWJM is particularly favored for cutting materials that are:

options.A: Heat sensitive and prone to thermal distortion/cracking with conventional or thermal methods
options.B: Extremely soft rubber only

questions.question: The nozzle (water) orifice in AWJM is typically made of:

options.B: Rubber

questions.question: Garnet abrasive is preferred in AWJM because it is:

options.B: Cost-effective, hard, and gives good cutting performance

questions.question: The kerf produced in AWJM cutting is typically:

options.B: Narrow, typically around 0.8-1.5 mm depending on parameters

questions.question: AWJM is considered environmentally favorable mainly because:

options.B: It uses water and natural abrasives with minimal hazardous fumes/heat generation
options.C: It produces large amounts of smoke
options.D: It requires no water at all

questions.question: A main process parameter affecting AWJM performance is:

options.B: Color of workpiece

questions.question: AWJM can cut thick stainless-steel plates primarily due to:

options.B: High kinetic energy of abrasive particles carried by the high-pressure water jet causing erosion

questions.question: Compared to laser cutting, AWJM has the advantage of:

options.B: Being a cold cutting process with no thermal distortion

questions.question: AWJM is generally NOT recommended for:

options.B: Machining materials that dissolve or degrade rapidly in water

questions.question: In AWJM, orifice wear over time leads to:

options.B: Reduced jet quality/coherence, requiring orifice replacement

questions.question: AWJM finds application in machining delicate materials like:

options.A: Titanium foam and composite laminates without delamination
options.B: Only cast iron

questions.question: Ultrasonic Machining uses which form of energy for material removal?

options.B: Mechanical vibration energy at ultrasonic frequency driving abrasive particles

questions.question: The typical frequency of vibration used in USM is:
In USM, material is removed mainly by:

options.B: Micro-chipping/erosion by abrasive slurry particles hammered by a vibrating tool

questions.question: The tool in USM is connected to which component that converts electrical signal to mechanical vibration?

options.B: Motor only

questions.question: The horn (concentrator) in USM is used to:

options.B: Amplify the vibration amplitude from the transducer to the tool tip

questions.question: USM is best suited for machining:

options.A: Soft ductile metals like aluminum and copper
options.B: Hard, brittle, non-conductive materials like glass, ceramics, quartz, and carbides

questions.question: The abrasive slurry used in USM typically consists of abrasive particles suspended in:

options.B: Water (or another liquid) as a carrier

questions.question: Common abrasives used in USM slurry include:

options.A: Boron carbide, silicon carbide, aluminum oxide
options.B: Sodium chloride

questions.question: Typical amplitude of tool vibration in USM ranges around:
In USM, the static feed force (tool pressure on workpiece) affects:

options.A: Only the color of the tool
options.B: Material removal rate and tool wear

questions.question: Magnetostrictive transducers used in USM are generally:

options.A: Highly efficient with no heat generation
options.B: Less efficient than piezoelectric transducers and generate more heat, requiring cooling

questions.question: USM is particularly effective for machining:

options.A: Through-holes and complex cavity shapes in brittle materials
options.B: Only external turning operations

questions.question: Tool materials in USM are generally chosen to be:

options.A: Softer and tougher than the workpiece to reduce relative tool wear
options.B: As brittle as the workpiece

questions.question: Tool wear in USM occurs due to:

options.B: Continuous abrasive particle impact against the tool tip

questions.question: In USM, increasing the abrasive grain size generally:

options.A: Increases MRR but worsens surface finish
options.B: Decreases MRR and always improves surface finish
options.C: Has no effect on MRR or finish

questions.question: USM is generally not suitable for machining:

options.B: Soft and ductile metals (low MRR and poor results)

questions.question: The main function of the abrasive slurry circulation system in USM is to:

options.A: Supply and circulate fresh abrasive slurry to the cutting zone continuously
options.B: Cool the transducer only

questions.question: Advantages of USM include:

options.A: Ability to machine hard, brittle, non-conductive materials with good accuracy and no thermal damage
options.B: Extremely high MRR compared to all NTM processes

questions.question: A limitation of USM is:

options.A: Excellent for high MRR in metals
options.B: Relatively low MRR, especially in ductile/tough materials, and tool wear

questions.question: In USM, the shape of the machined cavity generally corresponds to:

options.A: A random shape unrelated to tool geometry
options.B: The shape of the tool tip (reverse replica of the tool profile)
options.C: Always a circular hole regardless of tool shape

questions.question: The frequency generator/oscillator in a USM setup is used to:

options.B: Generate a high-frequency electrical signal that drives the transducer

questions.question: In USM, the term 'static load' refers to:

options.A: The constant downward force applied on the tool during machining
options.B: The vibration amplitude

questions.question: USM is often used for machining:

options.A: Tungsten carbide dies, ceramic components, and semiconductor wafers
options.B: Rubber gaskets

questions.question: Increasing the abrasive concentration in the slurry up to an optimum level in USM:

options.B: Generally increases MRR up to an optimum point, then may decrease due to slurry congestion

questions.question: Compared to AJM and AWJM, USM is unique because it uses:

options.A: A vibrating tool that hammers abrasive particles onto the workpiece rather than propelling them via a gas/water jet
options.B: Only chemical dissolution
